material_definitions: The electrical properties and the crystal structure were investigated for the ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The conductivity enhanced by the Li20 addition with LiHf2 (PO4) 3 system and by the increase ofx for Lil +xMxHf2\_x (PO4) 3 (M = Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu or Y) systems.
The P21/n monoclinic phase transformed to NASICON-type R3c rhombohedral phase at above 1173 K.
The activation energy for Li 	 ion migration was decreased by the phase transition.

The study focuses on the LiHf2(PO4)3 + yLi2O system, where Li2O acts as a flux to achieve high density and promotes the formation of the highly conductive NASICON-type R3c phase upon sintering above 1293 K.
This phase transition from the monoclinic P21/n phase is the primary driver of conductivity enhancement.
The maximum total conductivity was obtained for the LiHf2(PO4)3+0.1Li2O sample sintered at ca. 1298 K.
The electrical properties were studied for the ceramic electrolytes based on LiHf2(PO4)3.
The NASICON system studied here is Li(1+x)M(x)Hf(2-x)(PO4)3, where M=Cr, Fe, Sc, In, Lu, or Y.
The samples were sintered above 1293 K to obtain maximum conductivity and high density pellets.
The NASICON-type structure (R3c) was formed for all samples, with a small P21/n monoclinic phase remaining as secondary phase for some.
The maximum conductivity was obtained for x=0.2 or 0.3 in the Li(1+x)M(x)Hf(2-x)(PO4)3 system.
